description: An assistant principal must finalize a six-week cell-phone policy pilot for the high school, including its grade scope, storage procedure, safety-plan exception, launch date, and implementation records, with input from a ninth-grade teacher, a school counselor, and the technology coordinator.

shared_context.S1: The high school is planning a six-week pilot to reduce classroom disruptions caused by student cell-phone use.
shared_context.S2: The draft proposal covers grades 9 and 10, suggests placing phones in open classroom bins, and lists September 2, 2026, as the tentative launch date.
shared_context.S3: Ms. Brooks has authority to approve the pilot's final scope, procedures, and launch record.
shared_context.S4: At the weekly implementation meeting, Ms. Brooks routinely asks the participating teacher, counselor, and technology coordinator to report any operational information before she approves a student-facing procedure.

PF1.text: Mr. Ellis's classroom trial with all 9th-grade sections recorded 23 phone-related interruptions in two weeks, while numbered locking pouches reduced interruptions; he recommended a grade-9-only pilot using one pouch per student in his team notes, but the notes have not been added to the draft proposal.

PF2.text: Two students have active safety plans requiring them to receive time-sensitive messages from their caregivers during the school day; Ms. Romero confirmed the plans with both families this week, but the exception has not been entered in the pilot procedure.

PF3.text: The student-information system's phone-registration module will not be ready until September 16, 2026, and the technology change plan requires the pilot to launch with a digital registration record on that date; Mr. Shah confirmed the deployment date with the district systems team this week, but the draft still shows September 2.

acceptance_conditions: The pilot must cover grade 9 only.
Phones must be stored in one numbered locking pouch per student.
Students with active safety plans must be allowed to retain access for time-sensitive caregiver messages.
The pilot must launch on September 16, 2026.
A classroom storage-procedure commitment must be recorded.
A digital registration-record commitment must be recorded.

decisive_facts.why: The teacher's 9th-grade trial changes the pilot scope from grades 9 and 10 to grade 9 only and changes storage from open bins to one numbered locking pouch per student.
The two active safety plans change the procedure from no listed exception to allowing students with those plans to retain access for time-sensitive caregiver messages.
The confirmed systems deployment changes the launch date from September 2, 2026, to September 16, 2026, and requires a digital registration record.
